close_reason: Acknowledged. The 'mutated' boolean tracker at filenode.rs:191 is the right pattern: fetch state once at start, fetch again at end only if mutation observed. Per-iteration state fetches and unconditional re-fetches are both wrong for the documented reasons; preserve current shape.
description:
src/filenode.rs uses a 'let mut mutated = false;' tracker (line 187) that flips to true ONLY on observable backend mutations (Ok branches of create_object/destroy_object/update_object). The finalize_set_response helper (src/helpers.rs:69-76) then conditionally re-fetches state only when mutated is true.

This is the right shape: state token is fetched once at the start (old_state) and once at the end IF a mutation happened. It avoids the trap of fetching state per-iteration (which would be wrong if the backend bumps state during a failed operation) and avoids the trap of skipping state-refetch entirely on partial-success (which would return stale newState).

A future contributor might be tempted to either:
- Move state fetching to a per-call basis (causes incorrect newState reporting).
- Skip the mutated tracking and always re-fetch (wasted backend call when nothing changed).

Defend both behaviors. The current shape is the cheapest correct one.
title: Good: filenode.rs explicitly tracks 'mutated' flag for state monotonicity
